name: Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia, Kartagener Type
aliases: Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia with Situs Inversus

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: European Respiratory Society (ERS) Diagnostic Criteria for Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia

criteria.description: Presence of situs inversus or situs ambiguous
Chronic upper and lower respiratory tract infections including bronchiectasis
Demonstration of ciliary ultrastructural defects by electron microscopy or abnormal ciliary beat pattern by high-speed video microscopy
Identification of biallelic pathogenic variants in known PCD-associated genes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of chronic respiratory symptoms plus either ciliary ultrastructural defects or abnormal ciliary function confirmed by microscopy, with or without situs inversus
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Kartagener type is characterized by the triad of situs inversus, chronic sinusitis, and bronchiectasis.

pathognomonic.notes: Mirror-image reversal of thoracic and abdominal organs
Persistent inflammation of the paranasal sinuses
Permanent dilation of bronchi due to chronic infection

common.notes: Middle ear infections common in childhood
Nasal mucosal swelling and polyp formation
Clubbing of fingers due to chronic hypoxia

occasional.symptomName: Infertility in males due to immotile spermatozoa
occasional.notes: Impaired sperm motility leading to infertility
searchTerms: unable to conceive due to sperm immotility
lack of sperm movement causing infertility

occasional.notes: Coughing up blood due to bronchiectasis
Due to chronic infection and hypoxia

rare.notes: Rare association due to ciliary dysfunction in brain ventricles
Occasional cardiac malformations associated with situs abnormalities

laboratory: Abnormal ciliary beat frequency and pattern on high-speed video microscopy
Identification of pathogenic variants in DNAH5, DNAI1, and other PCD-associated genes
imaging: Sinus CT demonstrating chronic sinusitis and nasal polyps
Chest X-ray or abdominal ultrasound showing situs inversus
genetic: Biallelic mutations in genes encoding ciliary dynein arms (e.g., DNAH5, DNAI1)
Genetic confirmation supports diagnosis but absence does not exclude
other: Electron microscopy revealing absence or defects of dynein arms in cilia
Semen analysis showing immotile spermatozoa in affected males

distinguishingFeatures: Similar respiratory symptoms but no organ laterality defects

redFlags: Recurrent lower respiratory tract infections with bronchiectasis
Neonatal respiratory distress in term infant
Persistent nasal congestion and chronic sinusitis from early childhood
references: Lucas JS, et al. Diagnosis and management of primary ciliary dyskinesia. Eur Respir J. 2017;49(1):1601090.
Shapiro AJ, et al. Clinical features and diagnosis of primary ciliary dyskinesia. Pediatr Pulmonol. 2016;51(2):144-158.
